concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: מָקוֹם (the specific place where inspiration arrives)
דִּבּוּרִים שֶׁל תְּחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת (words of supplications and requests)
analysis_notes.summary: Torah #124 is a short practical teaching (eitza) about strengthening the moment of spiritual arousal in the very place it occurs, without moving. It contains no explicit bechina statements — no 'X is an aspect of Y' identifications. The concepts mentioned (hirhurei teshuva, histokkekut, makom, diburim of techinot) are described in a cause-and-effect / practical-advice framework rather than a parallel-nature framework. Therefore there are no bechina edges to extract and no packages to form. The concepts listed above appear in the source text but are not connected via bechina relationships.
